how: We read the website of every Denver wedding florist listed on Lazo (172 listings, 133 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: retail delivery shops, a flower preservation studio, a silk-flower rental company, and venues that were listed as florists. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: What is grown locally in my month? Front Range farm flowers run roughly April through November, and sun and dry air at altitude are hard on blooms, so ask what holds up outdoors.
Do you design for the venue, or deliver arrangements? Installation and teardown are the price difference.
Can I see one full wedding's florals at a budget like mine, not just a bouquet photo?

picks.name: Something Styled, Floral Design
picks.blurb: A boutique luxury wedding florist in Golden that designs for Colorado and Tennessee, playing with patterns and color palettes and mixing unusual elements with classic ones. Packages are tiered by need, from personals only (bouquets, boutonnieres and corsages) up through events under 50 guests and beyond.

picks.name: Flower Disco
picks.blurb: Steph, Chicago born and Denver based, came to flowers from interiors, upcycling and painting, and treats every wedding as one cohesive piece of art. Flower Disco takes only a select few weddings a year and designs worldwide.

picks.name: Sonora House Events (Formerly Hutson Floral Design)
picks.blurb: Formerly Hutson Floral Design, Sonora House is an intentionally small floral and planning studio taking a limited number of weddings each year, based in Colorado and Scottsdale. Florals start with a conversation about your vision rather than a catalog, for Denver, the mountains and destinations.

picks.name: Statice Floral
picks.blurb: Statice Floral's designer grew up on her family's sustainable flower farm and builds weddings around farm-fresh flowers from those same fields. A Lakewood studio with wedding collections laid out on the site, for couples who want the flowers to be local as well as pretty.

picks.name: Plume & Furrow
picks.blurb: Farmers and designers both, Plume & Furrow in Longmont sources most of its flowers from Front Range farms, with local blooms available April through November. Full-service weddings get a detailed consultation and custom palette, and a la carte wedding flowers are an option.

picks.name: Rose Bud Thorn
picks.blurb: Full-service weddings with Rose Bud Thorn start at a stated minimum of $8,000 and begin with a discovery call, a customized mood board and quoting options. Mack, originally from California's redwood coast, designs out of Boulder and is available for travel.

picks.name: Lalé Florals
picks.blurb: Founded in 2011 by Stephanie Buckallew, Lale Florals is a high-end Lakewood studio doing art-forward floral and event design, including decor and space-transforming installations. The house style, in its own words, is modern angles among soft petals: refined but bold.

picks.name: Belle Terre Floral
picks.blurb: Bold, art-forward florals for weddings and high-profile events in Boulder County and beyond, led by owner and designer Sarah Cioni out of Niwot. Belle Terre promises calm direction and sharp execution, built for events that need to look flawless on camera and in person.

picks.name: Buckley House of Flowers
picks.blurb: Buckley House of Flowers in Denver prints its minimums: bridal bouquets from $250, bridesmaid bouquets from $125, boutonnieres from $24 and corsages from $45 (before labor, design fee and tax). The team page is all personality, down to a Long Islander's bacon, egg and cheese loyalty.

picks.name: The Joyful poppy
picks.blurb: Rooted in Northern Colorado, The Joyful Poppy designs wedding and event florals across the state, from intimate elopements to large celebrations. The studio talks about beauty, authenticity and heart rather than a signature look, and keeps a blog and testimonials on the site.

picks.name: Marigolds Flowers
picks.blurb: A boutique floral and home goods shop in historic Idaho Springs that does full-service weddings for the mountain venues in its county, North Star Gatherings among them. Marigold also sells everyday flowers online, and talks about floral design as community as much as decor.

picks.name: Lilac and Sage Studio
picks.blurb: A Colorado native raised in the horticulture industry (an arborist father, a greenhouse seed-sower mother) runs this Loveland wedding and event floral studio. Lilac and Sage believes in transparency on pricing and makes a point of not wasting your planning time.
